### Bottom line
Over the last two fiscal years, **Netflix has grown revenue much faster than Disney**, roughly **15.9%** in the latest year and **15.7%** the year before, versus Disney's **3.4%** and **2.8%**. Netflix's top line expanded by about a third over the two years combined, while Disney's grew about 6%.

### Revenue by fiscal year

| Company | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Netflix (calendar FY, ends Dec) | $33.72B | $39.00B | $45.18B |
| Disney (FY ends late Sep) | $88.90B | $91.36B | $94.43B |

### Year-over-year growth

| Company | FY2024 vs FY2023 | FY2025 vs FY2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Netflix | +15.7% | +15.9% |
| Disney | +2.8% | +3.4% |

**Takeaway:** Netflix is compounding revenue in the mid-teens, driven by subscriber growth, price increases, and its ad tier. Disney's growth is low single digits as its legacy linear TV business declines even as streaming and parks contribute gains. Note the fiscal years don't align perfectly, Netflix's FY ends in December while Disney's ends in late September, but the growth gap is wide enough that the comparison holds.
